newsitem.title: USA: US Nov spot natgas falls ahead of holiday weekend.
newsitem.headline: US Nov spot natgas falls ahead of holiday weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for the remainder of November retreated Wednesday, as buyers anticipated a significantly lower industrial load and temperatures were forecast to moderate in the Midwest, sources said.
November gas on the Gulf Coast pipes traded mostly in the mid-$3.70s to low-$3.80s, down about 10 cents from Tuesday's levels, as suppliers dumped unneeded gas ahead of the long holiday weekend.
December prices in the Gulf were talked notionally in the mid-$3.80s, up from most bidweek levels.

At the New York city-gate, the drop in industrial loads over a holiday weekend outweighed the rise in heating demand. As a result, prices slumped into the $4.20s, down an average of 10-15 cents on the day.
Temperatures in the Northeast are expected to remain below-normal at least through the early part of next week.
In the Midcontinent, prices for the remainder of November fell by at least 10 cents to the low-to-mid $3.60s as milder weather moved into the region.

In west Texas, Permian gas traded mostly in the $3.50-3.55 range, down an average of 10 cents from Tuesday. Sources attributed the softening to warmer temperatures in Texas and greater supplies available to the California markets.
As a result of weaker Canadian prices, the southern California border market has been stagnant.
"The market has totally evaporated," one source said, noting the price discrepancy between Sumas and Permian basin prices.
"It doesn't make sense for California to buy Permian gas," she added.
Prices at Sumas, Wash., the U.S.-Canada export point, fell into the $2.20s per mmBtu late Tuesday, she noted.
Pacific Gas and Electric's 1,087 megawatt Diablo Canyon 1 nuclear power unit is expected to resume full service this Friday, a week after its automatic shutdown.
